body:
# Independent audit: finite-tilt attainment and projected active normals

The proposed compactification lemma is valid with the hypotheses
below. This note gives the complete audited argument, including the
separate role of actual anchor-fiber membership in its final step.

Let P be a finite nonempty set of base vectors in R^n, let d>=1, and
let each K_z be a compact full-dimensional convex body in R^d. Write
mu for the sum of their unnormalized d-volume measures. Fix any real
base j. For a unit continuous normal u and a continuous point x put

\[
 F(a,u,x)=\sum_{z\in P}
 |K_z\cap\{X:a\cdot(z-j)+u\cdot(X-x)\ge0\}|,
 \qquad G(u,x)=\inf_{a\in\mathbb R^n}F(a,u,x).
                                                               \tag{1}
\]

No integer-spacing or full-affine-rank assumption on P is needed.

## 1. Exact finite realization of a limiting cap mass

Consider a sequence `(a_k,u_k,x_k)` with `u_k->u_*` on the unit sphere
and `x_k->x_*`. After passing to a subsequence, every scalar
`a_k.(z-j)` has a limit in the compact extended real line. Let I
be the indices with finite limits, and let

`L=span{z-j:z in I}`.

The restrictions of a_k to L converge to a linear functional ell_*:
choose a basis of L among these finitely many vectors; convergence on
that basis determines convergence in operator norm on L. Identifying
functionals with vectors using the Euclidean inner product, this says

`P_L a_k -> ell_* in L`.

It also covers L={0}. Set

`a'_k=a_k-P_L a_k+ell_*`.

For every z in I the scalar `a'_k.(z-j)` is exactly its limiting
value. For every other z the scalar still diverges with its original
sign, because the correction tends to zero. A supposedly divergent
vector cannot belong to L, as its original projections would then be
linear combinations of the finite-limit basis projections.

On each finite-limit fiber, dominated convergence gives convergence of
the cap volumes to the cap with the limiting scalar and u_*,x_*.
The exceptional plane has d-volume zero because u_* is a unit vector.
On each divergent fiber, compactness of K_z and boundedness of x_k
make the original cap eventually the entire fiber or empty according
to that sign. There are only finitely many fibers.

Now choose one sufficiently large finite index k so that all divergent
fibers are likewise fully saturated for `(a'_k,u_*,x_*)`. The finite
fibers have already been assigned their exact limiting scalars.
Consequently the finite vector `a_*=a'_k` satisfies

\[
 F(a_*,u_*,x_*)=\lim_k F(a_k,u_k,x_k).                       \tag{2}
\]

There is no interchange of an infimum and a limit here: (2) explicitly
constructs a finite parameter attaining this particular subsequential
limit. Applying it to a minimizing sequence with fixed u,x proves
that the infimum in (1) is a minimum.

## 2. Joint continuity of the minimized cap function

For a fixed finite a, F is jointly continuous in `(u,x)` on the unit
sphere times R^d, by dominated convergence in every fiber. At a
limiting pair `(u_*,x_*)`, choose a minimizer a_* there. The inequality

`G(u_k,x_k)<=F(a_*,u_k,x_k)`

proves upper semicontinuity of G. For lower semicontinuity choose
minimizers a_k along a sequence realizing the liminf. Extract their
extended scalar limits and apply (2). Its finite realization gives

`G(u_*,x_*)<=liminf G(u_k,x_k)`.

Thus G is jointly continuous. Facet coincidences do not affect this
argument: every cutting plane remains null for the original d-volume,
and no continuity of section area at a supporting facet is asserted.

Choose R>0 so that every K_z lies in the Euclidean ball of radius R.
For a unit u, its scalar projection density is bounded by
`omega_(d-1) R^(d-1)`, since each section lies in a (d-1)-ball of
radius R. For d=1 the same assertion uses omega_0=1. Hence

\[
 |F(a,u,x)-F(a,u,x')|\le C\|x-x'\|,
 \quad C=|P|\omega_{d-1}R^{d-1},                           \tag{3}
\]

uniformly in a and u. Taking infima preserves this estimate for G.
This proves the required uniform Lipschitz continuity in x, without
boundedness of the selected minimizing tilts.

## 3. Vertical caps do not lower the infimum

A through-point vertical cap has a nonzero base normal b and is
`{b.(z-j)>=0}`. For any unit continuous u, choose a sufficiently
large finite positive A and take a=Ab in (1). At each base with
strictly positive or negative b-margin the new cap is respectively
full or empty; this follows from the minimum nonzero margin in the
finite list and the bounded continuous fibers. At zero-margin bases,
the nonvertical cap retains only a subset of the full fiber included
by the closed vertical cap. Its total mass is therefore no larger.

Every containing halfspace may first be shifted parallel until its
boundary passes through `(j,x)`, only decreasing its source mass.
Thus the infimum over ALL closed ambient halfspaces containing that
point equals

`D_j(x)=min_(|u|=1) G(u,x)`.

Continuity of G and compactness of the unit sphere show this minimum
is attained, and Section 1 supplies a finite corresponding tilt.
For n=0 there are no vertical caps, and the same conclusion holds.
The lemma requires d>=1 and makes no claim about the purely discrete
case, where no continuous unit normal exists.

## 4. Active projected normals balance at an interior fiber maximum

For this final step assume additionally that `j in P`, that
`x_* in int K_j`, and that x_* is a local maximum of D_j on K_j.
Put alpha=D_j(x_*) and

`A_*={u in S^(d-1):G(u,x_*)=alpha}`.

This active set is nonempty and compact by Section 2. We claim

\[
                        0\in\operatorname{conv}(A_*).       \tag{4}
\]

If not, strict separation supplies a vector v and delta>0 such that
`u.v>=delta` on A_*. On a neighborhood N of that compact set the
same inequality holds with delta/2. Choose a ball `B(x_*,r)` inside
the actual anchor fiber K_j. On that fiber the integer tilt is
identically zero, independently of a. Moving x_* to x_*-epsilon v
therefore adds, for every u in N and every tilt a, an own-fiber slab
of thickness at least epsilon delta/2. If epsilon|v|<=r/2, all its
cross-sections in that ball have (d-1)-volume at least
`omega_(d-1)(sqrt(3)r/2)^(d-1)`. Other fibers' caps also expand,
because the common threshold moves in the same favorable direction.
There is thus a constant c>0 such that

`F(a,u,x_*-epsilon v)>=F(a,u,x_*)+c epsilon`

uniformly in all a and all u in N. Taking minima over a gives the
same strict gain for G. On the compact complement of N, the old
G values have a uniform positive gap above alpha. Estimate (3)
preserves that gap under a sufficiently small move. Every direction
then has mass greater than alpha, contradicting local maximality.
The move stays in K_j because x_* is interior. This proves (4).

Carathéodory supplies at most d+1 active projected normals with a
positive convex dependence after discarding zero coefficients. Their
finite minimizing tilts exist by Section 1. No compactness of the
set of all such tilts is needed or claimed.

## Audit conclusion and exact limits

The finite-limit correction, joint continuity, vertical-cap comparison,
uniform Lipschitz estimate, and active-normal balance all pass. The
only additional hypothesis needed for the slab-balance conclusion is
the explicitly stated positive anchor fiber with x_* in its interior.
For an arbitrary real base j having no measured fiber, Sections 1--3
still hold, but the uniform own-fiber slab argument does not apply.
No hidden lattice rank, general-position, facet regularity, or
boundary-mass assumption enters the audited claims.
